Just the hush of settling dust... and the soft, steady grind of stone. Ch 4 – Extraction Dwight dove back into the rubble, tearing at loose stones with shaking hands. He tried for one of the heavier chunks, but his injured arm screamed in protest, the sharp throb in his wrist making it hard to lift, and the blood running down his palm left his grip weak and clumsy. He was aiming for the same gap he’d carved out earlier — hoping, praying it hadn’t fully collapsed. But the pile had shifted too far. Every reference point was gone. He was digging blind. It wasn’t until his third failed lift that he realized he was alone. He glanced up, confused — and saw Felix a few feet back, standing stiffly in the dust. His eyes were locked on the rubble, unfocused and distant, his posture rigid. One hand still held a small chunk of sandstone he hadn’t dropped. His fingers twitched around it absently, but the rest of him didn’t move. His chest rose and fell in quick, shallow bursts. Breathing too fast. Not blinking. Felix wasn’t frozen. He was folding . Quietly crumpling in on himself as the panic overtook him. “Felix!” Dwight’s voice cracked as he shouted across the rubble. “ Come on — get over here! ” No reply. Swearing under his breath, Dwight scrambled over, grabbing for Felix’s arm — only to find it stiff, locked in place like it didn’t belong to him. Up close, he could hear it: a soft murmur under Felix’s breath, looping fragments of thought, barely audible over the rasp of his shallow breathing. “It shouldn’t have collapsed... I made the call... I should have seen it—” His eyes weren’t tracking. He wasn’t blinking. Just staring through the pile like it was a grave he’d dug himself. Dwight’s stomach sank. Felix wasn’t just panicking. He was gone . Disassociating hard — caught in the guilt spiral, stuck in the feedback loop. If someone didn’t break him out of it fast, he was going to shut down completely. Panic flared — not at the rocks, but at Felix . At the distant stare, the static loop of words, the sinking posture. He’d seen it before. Survivors slipping inward. Folding in on themselves mid-trial, locked so deep inside they couldn’t hear their name shouted right beside them. Between the mental spirals and whatever the Fog did to people to prolong pain, some of them didn’t resurface for days. With Jill outside keeping Nemesis busy, if he didn’t do something fast, he was about to lose his only help. Something sparked in the back of his mind. Something he had seen other survivors do in moments like this. It didn’t always work, but... Before he could think about it too much and potentially talk himself out of it, he did the only thing he’d ever seen bring someone else around in a hurry. He slapped him. Hard. The sound cracked through the rubble louder than it should’ve — knuckles against cheekbone, clean and sharp. Felix hit the ground with a startled grunt, blinking up at Dwight in confused alarm. “Oh my god—oh my god I’m so sorry —I didn’t mean to—shit—I just— you weren’t there , I didn’t know what to do—are you okay??” Felix blinked again. Raised a hand to his cheek. “...Did you just hit me?” “I panicked!” Dwight squeaked. Felix stared at him for a second longer — then huffed a breath, somewhere between a laugh and a scoff. Dwight crouched down, offering a hand. “I didn’t mean to hit you that hard, I just... I needed help.” Felix took it, still half-stunned. “Help? Right, we were — shit , sorry... yeah, I’m ok.” The moment settled between them like dust, reorienting Felix back onto the pile as focus swept away whatever thoughts had tried to take him. If Dwight could break out of it, so could he. There was no time to dwell. The pile had shifted too much — David’s position could’ve been anywhere by now. What was once a half-buried incline off the staircase wall had slumped into something closer to a landslide: jagged, lopsided, and barely holding its shape. Each motion sent fine debris cascading across the surface like snow. Felix and Dwight dove back in, tearing away anything unstable — grabbing whatever stones looked like they’d cause trouble and chucking them down the slope. Dwight was working from memory, fingers bleeding from grit and broken edges, trying to trace the last place he’d touched David’s hand. The gap he’d made was gone. Swallowed up in the collapse. At least only the upper layers seemed to still be unstable, though. As he worked his way down, the larger stones seemed to have settled into something less chaotic, and could be worked around easily enough. It didn’t take long for him to have tunneled partway into the pile itself, managing to get nearly half his torso in, pilling smaller debris out and firing it behind him. David had been moving around a lot, but there was no way he had gotten that far from where he had been. If Dwight could re-open the area where he had last seen him, chances were good that he could find him again. Digging his fingers in around a good-sized chunk and wiggling it free, he finally spotted a flash of red fabric “I got him!” Dwight shouted. “I—I think I got him!” He cleared a ragged channel around the shape of an arm — elbow half-bent, the length vanishing under the bulk of jacket. He followed it upward, hand dragging through loose gravel and crumbled plaster, until his fingers brushed against something solid. Forehead. Cold and tacky with blood. “Felix — here!
